title: Claude Code plugin marketplace
description: Contract for .claude-plugin/marketplace.json at this repository's root: the storefront a consumer adds once (`/plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>`) so that installing and updating the framework stops being a copy a person performs and starts being a version the harness checks for. Source, retrieved 2026-08-29 from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces — the file sits at .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, `name`/`owner`/`plugins` are its required members, an entry's `source` may be a path relative to the marketplace's own root, and update checks read the version from the plugin's own manifest. What this record owns is fixed here: the storefront's identity and the one entry pointing at the assembled plugin. additionalProperties is false because this is a file Siegard authors rather than one it reads, and every optional member the harness would tolerate is a second home for a fact the plugin manifest already states.

name.description: The marketplace identity, and the suffix a consumer installs under: `/plugin install <plugin>@<this name>`. Kebab-case because it appears verbatim in that invocation. It names the storefront, not the plugin — this repository is the generator, so the storefront carries the repository's name and the plugin keeps its own.
Who answers for what this marketplace distributes. The maintainer, because publishing an entry here is the same act as shipping a release.

email.description: Where a consumer reaches the owner. Optional: an absent address is an owner reached through the repository instead, never a blank the harness fills.

plugins.description: The entries this storefront distributes. Exactly one: this repository assembles one plugin, and a second entry would be a distribution nothing in this repository authors or validates. An entry carries no `version` — the version has one home, the plugin's own manifest, and it is that manifest's bump the harness's update check reads; a version restated here would be a second value able to disagree with the one that ships.

name.description: The plugin's identity, equal to the `name` in its own manifest — the distribution suite pins the equality, because an entry naming a plugin the manifest does not is an install the consumer cannot resolve to what ran.

source.description: Where the plugin's root sits, relative to this repository's own root — the assembled distribution, `./dist/.claude`, whose `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is the manifest the harness reads. Relative because the marketplace and the plugin travel in one repository; an external source would be a distribution this repository's suite never validated.

description.description: What a consumer browsing the storefront reads before installing. Equal to the manifest's own description — the distribution suite pins the equality — because two prose homes for one identity are two that can disagree.
